main_text.p: & videte, quia non sum dæmonium incorporeum, quum, inquam, talia spectra, quale se[?] discipuli videre, autumabant, Dionysius Afer εἰδωλα appellet, simulacris homines magnitudine quoque, non modo specie, referentibus appellationem iftam ab eo tribui manifestum est.a Antiq. Ro. lib.6.{a} Dionysius Halicarnasseus narrat procerrimos duos adolescentes, qui victos ad Regillum lacum Latinos Romanis nunciaverant, quum nusquam postea comparárent, exi‑stimatos esse spectra sive εἰδωλα Castoris & Pollucis.b Sueton.Ca-lig.cap.22.{b} Quorum inanima item simulacra, inter quæ Caligula medium se adorandum adeuntibus exhibebat, nec dispari statuta fuisse infinuat idem Dionysius,c Antiq.Rom. lib.7.{c} quando simulacra Romana Græcis comparat: & εἰδωλα recte nuncupari, se judice, ostendit; utpote qui Deorum penatium imagines eodem quasi titulo insignit & honorat.d Paufan. in Attic. Arcad. &c.pasim.{d} Artemidorus ait Aegyptios coluisse feras & serpentes ut εἰδωλα Deorum: non magis parvum a magno distinguens voce εἰδωλα, quam Strabo voce εἴδος, quando Moses contra prædicat statuisse colendum Deum εἶδος χωρὶς, quo innuit, absque ulla imagine, magna, aut parva. Et quid commemorem plures? Namque si adjungerem Democritum,h Apud Sextum Empir. comment.l.8. c.de Diis.{h} Euclidem, Platonem, Bacchylidem, Lycophronem, Philonem, Iosephum, Arrianum, Dionem duos, Chrysostomum & Cassium, Plutarchū, Diogenianum, Stephanum Byzantium, Sextum Empiricum, Polyænum, Philippum, Maximum Tyrium, Galenum, Horapollinem,u De urbib. in voce, Iuov.{u} Ut in Cassandra, Iosephus, bello Iud.l.7.c.ult.
z Epigramm. Græcor lib.4.cap.9. in imaginem Medeæ.

page.notes: The scan is a page of a 17th-century Latin book with a good but slightly soft print. Marginal notes on the left are small and partly cut off at the edge, so several reference marks in the text are uncertain and were placed by position, not confirmed. The margin notes at "Aph-" and the footnote line placements are approximate. The Greek words (εἰδωλα, εἴδος, εἶδος, χωρὶς) are as seen, but accents may be misread. The main text line "quale se[?] discipuli" is uncertain. The passage "Ut in Cassandra, Iosephus, bello Iud.l.7.c.ult." is a poor reading of the lowest main-text lines and should be checked against the scan. The list of philosophers after "Namque si adjungerem" is partly illegible at the line ends.
